advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Catch `RefLockCorruptError` in `_pause_or_resume` (or translate it in `set_pause`) so `rebar bridge pause` against a corrupt gate exits cleanly instead of raising a traceback.
evidence: _ref_lock.py:81 `class RefLockCorruptError(ValueError):` — NOT a subclass of `RefLockError` (_ref_lock.py:73 `class RefLockError(RuntimeError):`)

set_pause reads/decodes any existing blob before writing: _ref_lock.py:692-695 `raw = _read_blob_bytes(...)` / `existing = _decode_pause(raw)` / `_decode_gate(raw)` — both `_decode_pause` and `_decode_gate` raise `RefLockCorruptError` on corrupt bytes (e.g. _ref_lock.py:647, 653, 657, 597, 603)

ABSENCE: the heldout suite covers `resume` over a corrupt blob (`test_resume_clears_corrupt_blob_without_decoding_then_pause_works`, which resumes first, then pauses on a clean gate) but has no test exercising `pause` invoked directly against a corrupt gate blob.
advisory.finding: `rebar bridge pause` against a pre-existing corrupt gate blob raises an uncaught `RefLockCorruptError` (a `ValueError`, not a `RefLockError`), producing an operator-visible traceback instead of a clean error.
scenarios: An operator runs `rebar bridge pause "reason"` while refs/reconciler/gate already holds a corrupt/partial blob (e.g. after a partial write or an out-of-band mutation) — the recovery path is `resume`, but they may reach for `pause` first.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `ref_lock.RefLockCorruptError` to the `except` tuple in `_pause_or_resume` (emitting the same corrupt-gate recovery guidance), or have `set_pause` re-raise decode failures as `RefLockError`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update docs/exit-codes.md `bridge` row Not-OK column to reflect that `pause`/`resume` exit 1 on configuration/CAS errors.
evidence: docs/exit-codes.md: `| \`bridge\` | 0 | — | — | no ticket id; \`preview\` shows proposed Jira changes, \`sync\` applies them, and \`pause\`/\`resume\` control scheduled reconciliation |`
src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py `_pause_or_resume`: `sys.stderr.write(f"Error: bridge pause/resume requires configured remote {remote!r}\n"); return 1`

src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py: `sys.stderr.write("Error: bridge pause requires a configured git user.email\n"); return 1` and `except (ref_lock.RefLockError, ref_lock.RefLockTimeoutError) as exc: ... return 1`
advisory.finding: docs/exit-codes.md keeps the `bridge` row's Not-OK column as `—` (no non-zero exit) while the same change adds pause/resume error paths that `return 1` — the documented exit contract now contradicts the code.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the `bridge` row's Not-OK column from `—` to `1` and note that pause/resume return 1 on missing remote, missing git user.email, or a conflicting pause.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a table-driven test feeding `_ref_lock.read_pause`/`_decode_pause` well-formed-JSON-but-invalid-pause-schema blobs (non-dict, extra/missing field, wrong gated_mode, paused:false, empty/non-string reason/who/paused_at) and asserting each raises RefLockCorruptError.
evidence: _ref_lock.py:648-657 the corrupt-detection branches: `if not isinstance(doc, dict)`, `if set(doc) != set(_PAUSE_FIELDS) or doc.get("gated_mode") != "reconcile-check"`, `if doc["paused"] is not True or any(not isinstance(doc[name], str) or not doc[name] ...)`
search: `_decode_pause` in tests → (no matches); `read_pause` in tests → only the orchestrate MagicMock patch, not a real malformed-schema call

tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_cli_heldout.py test_real_corrupt_gate_... plants `b"{corrupt"` (invalid JSON, hits the json.JSONDecodeError branch only); test_resume_clears_corrupt_blob... plants `b"not-json\x00gate"` but resume uses clear_gate which never decodes
ABSENCE: the workflow-lint malformed-marker tests exercise the BASH marker parser (a separate reimplementation), not the Python `_decode_pause`
advisory.finding: The new `_ref_lock._decode_pause` schema-validation fail-closed branches (non-dict JSON, wrong field-set, gated_mode != 'reconcile-check', paused not literally True, empty/non-string reason/who/paused_at) have no Python-level test. `read_pause`/`_decode_pause` is only tested against invalid JSON (`{corrupt`) at the integration boundary; a well-formed-JSON-but-invalid-pause-schema blob is never fed to it, so a regression that accepted (or failed to fail-closed on) e.g. `paused:false`, a missing `paused_at`, or an extra field would go undetected.
scenarios: A future edit relaxes `_decode_pause` validation (e.g. treats a missing paused_at or paused:false as a valid/None result) and the reconciler silently mis-reads or crashes instead of failing closed
advisory.suggested_fix: In tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock_ref_backend.py add a parametrized test that plants each malformed pause blob at GATE_REF and asserts `pytest.raises(ref_lock.RefLockCorruptError)` from `ref_lock.read_pause(repo)`, plus one asserting `advisory.read_pause` re-raises it as `ReconcileGateError`.
